messages:
Jade (Support): forwarding from customer — they see intermittent 429s while ingesting ~200k embeddings, plus some 401s when rotating keys. hitting free-tier ceiling? they said billing page shows 'payment required' for last invoice. asking for a short-term burst so demo doesn't fail :worried:
Tara (Support): thanks, passing to infra & billing. can you paste a short repro (curl + headers) and any X-RateLimit headers they got?
Jade (Support): pasted logs from customer:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
X-Request-ID: req_7a1
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1670001234
=== later ===
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```
they say they rotate keys every 30s with a script to avoid single-key concurrency limit. still gets 401s after rotation sometimes.
Kenji T: 429s + 401s pattern often means they hit plan concurrency + billing hold triggered token disable. billing-bot should show any invoice blocks. @BillingBot can you confirm account state for acct_id: acct_42?
BillingBot: acct_42 — last invoice failed (card expired) on 2026-01-22, account moved to soft-hold; API keys remain active but concurrency reduced to free-tier baseline (concurrency=2) and burst disabled.
Ryan (Sales): tagging in — we can offer a temporary burst uplift for demos. need start/end and expected qps. standard manual uplift window is 72h.
Jade (Support): customer asks for 24h uplift, targeting 10 QPS sustained, spike to 40 QPS for 10m windows, for a hackathon demo tomorrow. also wants guidance to avoid 401 during key rotation.
Tara (Support): proposed immediate steps for customer:
- hold off automated key rotation for now (rotation sometimes hits race conditions where key is removed server-side)
- implement client-side jitter/backoff (exponential) on 429s
- surface X-RateLimit-* headers and backoff until X-RateLimit-Reset
- if they have multiple team keys, spread requests across them but keep per-key QPS under plan concurrency
Kenji T: additional notes — for embeddings batched uploads, recommend batching size 64 and keep parallel requests <= 8. use /v1/embeddings?model=... with streaming disabled to reduce overhead.
Alex W: for 401s specifically, check rotation flow: when creating a new key we recommend a warmup window where both old+new are accepted for 60s. if their script immediately deletes old key, they'll see auth failures if any in-flight requests use old key.
Jade (Support): shared a short curl repro the customer uses to rotate quickly:
```
# rotate.sh (simplified)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys -d '{"label":"tmp"}'
# get new key
export KEY=new_key
# delete old key
curl -X DELETE https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/old_id -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
# start heavy ingest
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d "$PAYLOAD" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings & done
```
Customer said deletion sometimes races with inflight requests.
Ryan (Sales): if billing approves temporary uplift we can enable a 72h burst token; for 24h we can do a short exception but need billing clearance. Ryan will confirm by EOD.
BillingBot: to unblock immediately — customer can update card on billing portal: https://billing.redwood.ai/acct_42/update-card ; once charge succeeds we can restore normal concurrency (paid plan).
Tara (Support): interim workaround we can enable (manual, ops) — create a one-off ephemeral key scoped to higher concurrency and expiry 24h; required approval from sales + billing. Ryan are you OK to approve ephemeral key if billing can't update today?
Ryan (Sales): OK to approve ephemeral key for 24h once we have a signed confirmation email from the customer and we log the uplift in the sales tracker. I'll DM Jade for the email copy. :thumbsup:
Kenji T: ops note — if we create ephemeral key, set backend to accept old key for 120s and queue delete until TTL expires to avoid 401 race. also set quota on that key rather than account-level to contain risk.
Jade (Support): will relay steps. customer asked about long-term: they want to upgrade to paid monthly but have procurement delay. asked if there's a grace window.
Ryan (Sales): we can open a sales-assisted path: 14-day provisional paid access with invoice on file, requires signed MSA for enterprise. for SMB we have a credit card on file option. I'll send the invoice link.
Alex W: followups for engineering — if this pattern repeats we should add a short guidance doc in support playbooks: "key rotation best practices" and include server-side warmup for 2 minutes and clearer 429 reason codes (concurrency vs burst). filing a small docs task.
Jade (Support): thanks everyone. tagging next steps: 1) billing link to customer, 2) Ryan to confirm ephemeral key approval, 3) Kenji/ops to prepare ephemeral key with quotas, 4) support to send repro/backoff guidance to customer.
Ryan (Sales): confirmed, I'll DM Jade and mark sales tracker.
Tara (Support): marking resolved pending billing update, will reopen if uplift needed. :white_check_mark:
support-bot: incident-note created: #INC-2026-0421 — temporary-burst-request — assigned to Ryan, Kenji, BillingBot
Jade (Support): customer acknowledged and will try card update now. will follow up if still seeing 429s. :ok_hand:
